Projections of revenues are sensitive to underlying eco­ nomic conditions, administrative actions and how policies are implemented, and how taxpayers respond to them.

Federal agencies take administrative actions to imple­ ment laws and programs under their authority that affect tax receipts. For example, administrative actions throughout 2025 increased tariff rates, on net. That sig­ nificantly increased revenue from customs duties. Other administrative actions taken in 2025 have resulted in decreases in net immigration that likely reduced income, payroll, and excise taxes. For decades, tariff policies remained fairly stable. During that time, CBO’s baseline projections of customs duties were based on a relatively simple model that began with recent trade data and extrapolated later collections of customs duties by using projections of total imports and adjusting for scheduled statutory changes in tariff rates. Beginning in 2018, the Administration imposed higher tariff rates on certain goods, particularly those imported from China. Rates rose again in 2025 after the Administration levied broad-based tariffs on most imports into the United States. Since then, tariff policies have changed frequently. In response, CBO invested significant resources to review its methods for mod­ eling tariffs and to develop an improved model that better accounts for shifting incentives for individuals and businesses to substitute imports among countries and products that are subject to differing tariff rates. 40 CBO continues to evaluate customs duties collections and adjusts each new baseline to account for observed changes in patterns of imports.
